clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old patient presented with a 1-year history of left scrotal swelling complicated by local hyperemia and pain. History included cryptorchidism with surgery in childhood. Physical exam revealed a 6/15 cm hard, intensely painful left testicular tumor with inflamed adjacent tissues. Laboratory tests showed elevated inflammatory markers (WBC 16500/dl, ESR 74 mm/h, fibrinogen 1084 mg/dl, alkaline phosphatase 937 UI/l). Ultrasonography displayed structural modifications characteristic of testicular malignancy with no regional adenopathies. Histopathologic examination (implied but exact report text not available) confirmed seminoma with cribriform and pseudoglandular patterns and localized T2N0 staging. The postoperative course was uneventful with referral to oncology. Serum tumor markers and staging imaging beyond ultrasound were ordered but not documented in the source material.
